title: PREPING: Zero-Task Agent Memory Construction via Self-Practice
abstract: arXiv:2605.13880v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Agent memory is typically constructed either offline from curated demonstrations or online from post-deployment interactions. However, regardless of how it is built, an agent faces a cold-start gap when first introduced to a new environment without any task-specific experience available. In this paper, we study pre-task memory construction: whether an agent can build procedural memory before observing any target-environment tasks, using only self-generated synthetic practice. Yet, synthetic interaction alone is insufficient, as without controlling what to practice and what to store, synthetic tasks become redundant, infeasible, and ultimately uninformative, and memory further degrades quickly due to unfiltered trajectories. To overcome this, we present Preping, a proposer-guided memory construction framework. At its core is proposer memory, a structured control state that shapes future practice. translated_title: PREPING：基于自主练习的零任务智能体记忆构建
translated_abstract: 智能体记忆通常通过两种方式构建：要么离线基于精心策划的演示数据，要么在线基于部署后的交互。然而，无论采用哪种构建方式，当智能体首次进入一个没有任何任务特定经验的新环境时，都会面临冷启动鸿沟。本文研究了任务前记忆构建问题：即智能体能否在观察任何目标环境任务之前，仅利用自主生成的合成练习来构建程序性记忆。然而，仅靠合成交互是不够的，因为如果不控制练习什么内容以及存储什么内容，合成任务会变得冗余、不可行且最终缺乏信息量，而且由于未经过滤的轨迹，记忆还会进一步快速退化。为解决这一问题，我们提出了Preping，一个由提议者引导的记忆构建框架。其核心是提议者记忆，这是一种结构化的控制状态，用于塑造未来的练习方向。提议者生成合成任务……
tldr: 提出Preping框架，通过提议者记忆这一结构化控制状态引导智能体进行自主合成练习，使智能体在零任务经验的情况下预先构建程序性记忆，解决新环境中的冷启动问题。
en_tdlr: PREPING is a proposer-guided memory construction framework that enables agents to build procedural memory before encountering any target-environment tasks through controlled self-generated synthetic practice, addressing the cold-start gap in new environments.
